newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Private firm challenges Romanian state oil company.
newsitem.headline: Private firm challenges Romanian state oil company.

text.p: A private oil company has launched a legal attempt to dismantle Romania's state-run National Oil Company (CRP), saying it had created a monopoly in the troubled oil sector, a company executive said on Friday.
The CRP, created in July to consolidate Romania's oversized oil industry, dismissed the move as a "joke of the transition period".

"We have filed a lawsuit with the Bucharest Court of Appeal asking it to annul the government decision to create the CRP and have it dismantled," Teodor Vostinaru, president of General Trading & Investments Co SA (GTI), said.

GTI, through its GTI-Oil unit, is a major private oil operator. It is also one of the founders of Petrogas SA, set up as a counter to CRP to guard against what it said could be unhealthy monopoly practices.
The company launched the suit earlier this week and took out full-page advertisements in Bucharest dailies on Friday to explain its action.

The CRP groups 12 state-owned refineries, four transport and 41 oil distribution companies as well as a research institute and an oil exploration firm. It also administers Romania's sole oil terminal in the Black Sea port of Constanta.

It is supposed to provide funds for crude oil imports badly needed in Romania's energy-starved industries. But oil sector analysts say it is a top-heavy bureaucratic conglomerate and fear it will stall reform of the sector.

"We had plans to import 250,000 tonnes of crude monthly and we contacted the oil terminal, which said it needed CRP approval to handle our imports," Vostinaru said. "What more proof do you need that this is a monopoly?"
The CRP said it did nothing to hinder GTI's imports.

"We sent a letter to GTI saying it could undertake whatever activity it wanted," CRP Vice-President Ionita Vifor said by telephone. "The CRP welcomes cooperation with all operators in this sector just as it welcomes any oil imports."
Romania produces around 6.7 million tonnes of crude oil a year, but imports are needed to meet domestic demand.
Its 12 refineries have an annual capacity of 34 million tonnes but are grossly underused. They plan output of 14.5 million tonnes this year, down from 15.2 million in 1995.
The GTI lawsuit said Romania needed more than a single company for loyal competition, to bring in more raw materials and boost the quality of products, the GTI said in its lawsuit.
